newsitem.title: UK: Brit Gas hails Ofgas decision with caution.
newsitem.headline: Brit Gas hails Ofgas decision with caution.

text.p: British Gas welcomed the decision of regulator Ofgas not to widen the TransCo reference to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission, but the utility retained some reservation as a broader investigation is still possible.
"It is good to hear they don't intend to widen it and I hope they won't change their mind later," British Gas' deputy chairman Philip Rogerson told Reuters.

Ofgas said earlier it asked the MMC to investigate only the controversial price proposals for pipeline unit TransCo. But it added it might widen the probe later on the MMC's Request to vet structural changes at British Gas too.
This remark injected a note of caution into British Gas' reaction to the MMC reference.
"As a matter of precaution we clearly must plan on the possibility that it gets widened," Rogerson said.
But he played down fears that any wider investigation would seriously hamper British Gas' plans to split itself in two early in 1997.
"I don't think it would be disastrous at all," Rogerson said, adding it would merely mean extra work for British Gas.
Investigations by the MMC and by a parliamentory committee in respectively 1993 and 1995 suggested that the demerger plan would meet no opposition, he said.
"There is a huge amount of precendent that any widening would not be appropriate," Rogerson added.

British Gas plans to break itself up in a trading firm and a company called TransCo International, which would include the regulated transport activities as well as the foreign production and power generation operations.
Earlier press reports had suggested Ofgas might want the MMC to consider whether the two businesses within TransCo International should be separated.
